issues: Integrity: no problems found. The diff only changes how the basin-hopping perturbation works: 25% of the time it shifts a band of centers sideways, otherwise it moves 1-3 random circles as before. It adds no file or network access and pastes no coordinates. The packing is still computed and checked the same way.

Bugs: none found that would make the result meaningless. best_r is used for the median radius and only sets the step size. Clipping to [0,1] then re-optimising is the same as the original branch. A band can be empty, which just makes a no-op perturbation, so this is harmless.
Numbers: the candidate scored -2.6298 against the incumbent's -2.6360. Since lower loss is better, the candidate is about 0.0062 worse, and the provisional reject decision matches that.

Recomputing z: there is only one run on each side, so there is no sample variance to compute z from. The harness's z of -4400.692 matches a difference of about 0.0062 divided by a noise sd of about 1.41e-6 (roughly sqrt(2) x 1e-6). The gap from my figure of about -4384 comes from the shown values being rounded to 4 decimals. The size of z depends entirely on that assumed noise level, but the sign and the reject decision hold either way.

Suggestion: this is a single-seed comparison. The difference in this run probably comes mostly from which basin the seeded search lands in, not from the new move itself. Testing several seeds would show whether the shear move ever helps.
